messages:
Jay R: Quick heads-up — planned schema change for users.profile_bio tonight 22:00 UTC. This is a small ADD COLUMN + staged backfill against the primary shard. Expect potential short row-lock spikes during the backfill. I'll be on call for rollback decisions. deploybot will kick the canary at 22:00 and then promote if green.

Sam H: Ack. Which services need to be pinned during the window?

Jay R: Pin frontend and profile-service to v3.4.1 for the 30m window. We don't want consumers writing the new field until backfill is mostly done.

deploybot: Scheduled deploybot: canary job queued for 1759999288. Notifying eng-releases. :gear:

Laura K: I'll take lock-watch. I'll add a short query to tail pg_locks and alert if row-exclusive locks > 10 for > 2m.

Mike D: Rollback criteria I care about: any sustained >1s p99 for profile-service for 10m OR deadlock spike >5 in 5m. If hit, we abort backfill and fail open the schema flag.

Jay R: Agreed. Rollback steps (short):
```
1) Pause the backfill workers: /svcctl profile-backfill pause
2) Flip feature flag to old behavior: POST /admin/flags/schema_profile_bio false
3) If partial schema change required revert: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS profile_bio;
4) If needed, restore DB snapshot from pre-change (only if corruption suspected).
```

Sam H: Do we have a pinned migration artifact? I can upload an explicit SQL file to releases bucket and reference it in the deploy notes.

Jay R: Yes — uploaded as s3://releases/1759998888/profile_bio_add_v1.sql. We'll reference that in the deploy note and pin the migration hash in the deploy tooling (`migration_sha=3f7a2b`).

Laura K: I set an alert: 
`SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE mode LIKE '%RowExclusiveLock%' AND granted=true;`
If >10 for 120s I'll post in #eng-oncall and ping @Mike D.

Mike D: I'll be standing by to run the emergency kill if we see lock escalation: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid)` for the heavy hitters, then scale read replicas down to reduce contention.

Sam H: Noted. I'll pin profile-service to `v3.4.1` in deploybot and hold the auto-promote for 15m after canary success.

deploybot: Canary started at 1759999288 (canary id cb-764). Logs: https://deploys/redwood/cb-764. Status: running.

Jay R: Final checklist for tonight:
- [x] Migration SQL uploaded and sha noted
- [x] Feature flag created (`schema_profile_bio`)
- [x] Pin frontend/profile-service to v3.4.1
- [x] Lock-watch alert set (Laura)
- [x] Rollback steps documented and accessible

Laura K: 22:05 UTC canary looks fine, locks stable. Will keep 1min polling. :thumbsup:

Mike D: If anything weird shows up, I'll trigger the abort and we revert the flag. Otherwise standing by.

Sam H: Holding auto-promote until +15m after canary. I'll post status updates in this thread.

Jay R: Thanks team. If anyone is running late, call out now. Otherwise I will start the window at 22:00 and post the deploybot link here.

deploybot: Canary cb-764: completed healthy at 1759999380. Promoting to prod in 10m unless a rollback is requested.

Laura K: No anomalies in the first 10m. continuing monitor.

Sam H: Promote approved from my side at +12m. :white_check_mark:

Mike D: No rollback needed. Closing watch but keeping alerts on for next 30m.

Jay R: Promoted and feature-flag toggled to true for writes. Post-deploy note: backfill completed with 0 deadlocks, avg p95 latency unchanged. Great job.

Sam H: Added release note snippet: "users.profile_bio added; backfilled safely; pinned services during window."

deploybot: Deploy summary: canary cb-764 -> promoted. Tags: migration_sha=3f7a2b, rollback_flag=schema_profile_bio.

Jay R: Thread closed; archiving logs to s3://deploy-archive/1759998888/
